'''Ishfaq Ahmad''' (3 November 1930 – 18 January 2018) {{small|''[[Sitara-i-Imtiaz|SI]], [[Hilal-i-Imtiaz|HI]], [[Nishan-i-Imitiaz|NI]], [[Fellow of the Pakistan Academy of Sciences|FPAS]]''}}, was a [[Pakistani people|Pakistani]] [[nuclear physicist]], [[Professor emeritus|emeritus professor]] of [[High energy physics|high-energy physics]] at the [[National Centre for Physics]], and former [[Ministry of Science and Technology (Pakistan)#Science Advisors|science advisor]] to the [[Government of Pakistan]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Dr. Ishfaq Ahmad (N.I, H.I, S.I) Advisor S&T / Minister of State|url=http://www.pc.gov.pk/mos_profile.htm|publisher=Government of Pakistan|access-date=14 August 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121025031651/http://pc.gov.pk/mos_profile.htm|archive-date=25 October 2012|url-status=dead}}</ref>

A versatile [[theoretical physicist]],<ref name="Usman Shabbir published as cover story in Defence Journal (May 2004 issue)">{{cite web|last=Shabbir|first=Usman|title=Munir Ahmad Khan and PAEC's other achievements|url=http://www.defencejournal.com/2004-5/print/p-cvs.asp|website=The Multan Conference, 20 Jan 1972: The day the bomb was born|publisher=Usman Shabbir published as cover story in Defence Journal (May 2004 issue)|access-date=10 October 2012|location=Islamabad, Pakistan|page=1|quote=Dr. Ishfaq Ahmad (a theoretical physicist) and others involved in critical technologies and projects worked as a team, and gave ultimate security to Pakistan... Quoted by: Pakistan Defence Journal, 2004|archive-date=24 December 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181224213338/http://www.defencejournal.com/2004-5/print/p-cvs.asp|url-status=dead}}</ref> Ahmad made significant contributions in the theoretical development of the applications and concepts involving the [[High-energy physics|particle physics]], and its relative extension to the [[quantum electrodynamics]], while working as senior research scientist at the [[CERN]] in the 1960s and 1970s.  Joining the [[Pakistan Atomic Energy Commission|PAEC]] in the late 1950s, Ahmad served as the director of the Nuclear Physics Division at the secret [[Pakistan Institute of Nuclear Science and Technology|Pinstech Institute]] which developed the first designs of [[atomic bomb]]s, a clandestine project during the [[Indo-Pakistani War of 1971|post-1971 war]].<ref name="Rahman 1999 71–72">{{harv|Rehman|1999|pp=71–72}}</ref>  There, he played an influential role in leading the physics and mathematical calculations in the [[critical mass]] of the weapons, and did theoretical work on the implosion method used in the weapons.<ref name="Rahman 1999 78–80">{{harv|Rehman|1999|pp=78–80}}</ref>

Since the 1960s and onwards, he was a high-ranking official at the [[International Atomic Energy Agency|IAEA]] as part of the Pakistan Government's official mission, working to make the peaceful use of [[nuclear power]] for the industrial development. Having chaired the PAEC from 1991 until 2001, he was affiliated with the [[Pakistan Government]] as a science adviser to the [[Prime Minister of Pakistan|prime minister]] on [[Pakistan and weapons of mass destruction|strategic]] and [[Science in Pakistan|scientific programs]], with the status of [[Minister of State]]. A vehement supporter for the peaceful use of nuclear energy, he earned public and international fame in May 1998 when he oversaw and directed PAEC to perform country's first public [[atomic test]]s (see [[Chagai-I]] and [[Chagai-II]]) in a secret [[Ras Koh|weapon-testing laboratories]] in [[Baluchistan (Pakistan)|Balochistan Province]] of Pakistan.<ref>{{harv|Rehman|1999|pp=18–20}}</ref> He died on 18 January 2018, aged 87 in Lahore.<ref>{{cite news|title=Famed nuclear scientist Ishfaq Ahmed passes away|url=https://www.samaa.tv/pakistan/2018/01/famed-nuclear-scientist-ishfaq-ahmed-passes-away/|access-date=23 January 2018|publisher=Samaa TV|date=19 January 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|title=Renowned nuclear scientist 'Dr Ishfaq Ahmad' laid to the rest|url=https://www.businessplustv.pk/2018/01/renowned-nuclear-scientist-dr-ishfaq-ahmad-laid-rest/|access-date=23 January 2018|work=Business Plus|date=21 January 2018}}{{Dead link|date=January 2026 |bot=InternetArchiveBot }}</ref>

==Biography==

===Early life and education===

Ahmad was born in [[Gurdaspur]], [[Punjab (British India)|Punjab]] in [[British India|India]] on 3 November 1930 into a [[Kakazai]] family that had long been settled in Punjab.<ref name=express>{{Cite web |last=Rahi |first=Arwin |date=2020-02-25 |title=Why Afghanistan should leave Pakistani Pashtuns alone |url=https://blogs.tribune.com.pk/story/94157/why-afghanistan-should-leave-pakistani-pashtuns-alone/ |access-date=2020-06-26 |website=The Express Tribune |language=en-US |archive-date=3 May 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200503132315/https://blogs.tribune.com.pk/story/94157/why-afghanistan-should-leave-pakistani-pashtuns-alone/ |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name="The Office of Pakistan Academy of Sciences"/><ref name="Kakazai">{{Cite news|url=https://www.dawn.com/news/1365402|title=The history of Lahore's Kakayzais|last=Sheikh|first=Majid|date=2017-10-22|work=Dawn|location=Pakistan|access-date=2018-02-28|language=en-US|archive-date=19 January 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240119052126/https://www.dawn.com/news/1365402|url-status=live}}</ref> Ahmad obtained his early education in [[Jalandhar]], later schooling in [[Faisalabad|Lyallpur]], and [[Lahore]] before enrolling in the [[University of Punjab|Punjab University]] in [[Lahore]] to study [[Physics]], and earned his undergraduate, [[Bachelor of Science|BSc]] degree, in [[Physics]] in 1949.<ref name="The Office of Pakistan Academy of Sciences">{{Cite web
  | last =(PAS)
  | first =Pakistan Academy of Sciences
  | author-link =Pakistan Academy of Sciences
  | title =Fellow: Dr. Ishfaq Ahmad-PAS
  | website =The Office of Pakistan Academy of Sciences
  | year =2012
  | url =http://www.paspk.org/detail.php?id=16&id1=66
  | access-date =12 October 2012
  | archive-date =24 December 2018
  | archive-url =https://web.archive.org/web/20181224213335/http://www.paspk.org/detail.php?id=16&id1=66%20%20
  | url-status =dead
  }}.</ref>

After entering in the post graduate school at the Punjab University, Ahmad obtained his [[Master of Science|MSc]] degree, in 1951, after submitting his master's thesis on nuclear physics, which was supervised by [[Rafi Muhammad Chaudhry|R. M. Chaudhry]].<ref>{{cite web
 | website =Pride of Pakistan
 | title =Career of Tahir Hussain
 | url =http://www.prideofpakistan.com/v2/index.php/national-heroes/1954-dr-tahir-hussain
 | access-date =11 October 2012
 | archive-date =11 February 2013
 | archive-url =https://web.archive.org/web/20130211053752/http://www.prideofpakistan.com/v2/index.php/national-heroes/1954-dr-tahir-hussain
 | url-status =dead
 }}</ref> With his master's degree, he obtained [[Honors student|Honours diploma]] and secured a [[gold medal]]lion for the recognition of his work in physics.<ref name="The Office of Pakistan Academy of Sciences"/> He taught various undergraduate physics laboratory courses at the [[Government College University, Lahore|Government College University]] while working on fundamental concepts in nuclear physics with his university mentor. In 1954, he won the scholarship under the [[Colombo Plan]] fellowship program and went to [[Quebec]], Canada for his doctorate studies.<ref name="McGill University">{{Cite web
  | last =Rehman
  | first =Mumtazul Haque
  | title = Appendix
  | website = Montreal Religious Sites Project
  | publisher =[[McGill University]]
  | url = http://mrsp.mcgill.ca/reports/html/MuslimHistory/index.htm#100
  | access-date =25 April 2010 }}
</ref>

Ahmad attended the doctorate school at the [[Université de Montréal]] and did a two-year-long course in [[Particle physics]] and engaged his research on theoretical physics. In 1959, Ahmad obtained [[Doctor of Science|D.Sc.]] in [[Nuclear physics|physics]] after submitting his doctoral works on concepts on advancing on particle physics.<ref name="McGill University"/> His theses were written in fluent [[French language|French]] and English language, and he reluctantly returned to Pakistan under the terms of Colombo Plan contract. His [[Doctor of Science|DSc]] theses were supervised by [[:fr:Pierre Demers (physicien)|Pierre Demers]]<ref name="Demers Group of Physics">{{cite web|last1=Demers|first1=Pierre|title=Decade 1950–59|url=http://www.er.uqam.ca/nobel/c3410/PierreDemersBibl.html|publisher=Demers Group of Physics|access-date=8 November 2014|archive-date=17 August 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140817201251/http://www.er.uqam.ca/nobel/c3410/PierreDemersBibl.html|url-status=dead}}</ref> and covered a wide range of research in the study of [[elementary particle]]s by using the deployment of special fine grain nuclear emulsion ([[Silver bromide|AgBr]]).<ref name="Demers Group of Physics"/> During his long doctoral studies, Ahmad studied nuclear reaction at the [[Montreal Laboratory]] with supervisors and scientists role in the [[Manhattan Project]]. Upon his return to Pakistan, he joined the [[Pakistan Atomic Energy Commission]] (PAEC) as a senior scientist.<ref name="McGill University"/>

===Academia and CERN===

In 1952, Ahmad served as a [[visiting professor]] of mathematics at the [[Government College University, Lahore|Government College University]], before accepting the professorship of mathematics at the [[University of Paris]] in 1959.<ref>{{Cite web
  | last =Friends
  | first =The Successful Pakistan in and Around the World
  | title =See:Prof. Ishfaq Ahmad
  | website =friendskorner.com
  | url =http://www.friendskorner.com/forum/f39/successful-pakistanis-around-world-8830/
  | access-date =22 May 2010
  | archive-date =7 May 2010
  | archive-url =https://web.archive.org/web/20100507192605/http://www.friendskorner.com/forum/f39/successful-pakistanis-around-world-8830/
  | url-status =dead
  }}</ref> He engaged his research in theoretical physics and obtained a one-year-long research fellowship at the [[Institute for Theoretical Physics, Copenhagen|Niels Bohr Institute for Theoretical Physics]].<ref>{{Cite web
 |author        = Dr. Ishfaq Ahmad 
 |title       = Minister Planning Commission: Dr. Ishfaq Ahmad (N.I, H.I, S.I)
 |website        = [[Planning Commission (Pakistan)|Planning Commission of Pakistan]]
 |publisher   = Jawaid Azfar, Computer Centre of Planning Commission
 |url         = http://115.186.133.3/pcportal/mos_profile.htm
 |url-status     = dead
 |archive-url  = https://archive.today/20100410204827/http://115.186.133.3/pcportal/mos_profile.htm
 |archive-date = 10 April 2010}}
</ref> In 1962–64, he accepted the professorship in physics at the [[University of Montreal]] and the [[University of Ottawa]]. In Ottawa, he carried out pioneering research in [[Resonance (particle physics)|particle resonance]] and published important publications in theoretical physics.<ref>{{cite journal|last=Ahmad|first=Ishfaq |display-authors=etal |title=Resonance in the Nucleus|journal=Progress of Theoretical Physics|year=1966|volume=35|issue=1–3|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=NcgzAAAAIAAJ&q=Ishfaq+Ahmad+Pion|access-date=11 October 2012}}</ref>

Ahmad also performed experiments on nuclear physics at the [[Meuse/Haute Marne Underground Research Laboratory|Meuse Underground Laboratories]] of [[France]].<ref>{{Cite web
  | last1=(NPT)
  | first1=Nazaria-i-Pakistan Trust
  | author2=Khalid Mahmood Asim
  | title=Dr. Ishfaq Ahmad
  | website=Prominent Scientists of Pakistan
  | year=2003
  | url=http://nazariapak.info/famous-pakistanis/Scientists.html
  | access-date=25 April 2010
  | archive-date=13 January 2010
  | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100113154236/http://www.nazariapak.info/famous-pakistanis/Scientists.html
  | url-status=dead
  }}</ref> In 1965, Ahmad published a research report on absorption of Pion's [[cross section (physics)|cross sections]] and the range of complex atom's energy of the pion particle.<ref name="EUROPEAN ORGANIZATION FOR NUCLEAR RESEARCH">{{cite web|last=Ishfaq Ahmad|title=Í ABSURPTIÜN ÜF FAST Tt MESÜNS IN NUCLEAR EMULSIUN|url=https://docs.google.com/viewer?a=v&q=cache:_3dFmOAq85oJ:cdsweb.cern.ch/record/1117271/files/CM-P00073663.pdf+Ishfaq+Ahmad+Absorption+of+Fast+%CF%80%C2%B1+Mesons+in+Nuclear+Emulsion&hl=en&gl=us&pid=bl&srcid=ADGEEShZ_-mo8gbLzLPyEr7WTL3elRKO4z3zTzJWV_hqloVsUGJoGP9I9nCN4f9WY-B7n7sFx0Q4qSaBtHFU3Ix8mQb0o4HnGiNBqS9bLc-2NaMhomkAvaOJjea1NtOkG1JclfS0rCR9&sig=AHIEtbSrIJKVlV-r0bCEbJkEZ36lHXS-bQ|publisher=EUROPEAN ORGANIZATION FOR NUCLEAR RESEARCH}}</ref> He recalled his Cern experience in 1994:

{{blockquote|text=In 1994, I visited [[CERN]] as chairman of [[Pakistan Atomic Energy Commission|PAEC]]. The visit took place on the initiative of Pakistani ([[Theoretical Physics|theoretical]]) [[physicist]] Ahmed Ali, who works at [[Deutsches Elektronen-Synchrotron|DESY]]. It brought back good memories of my earlier visits, which date back to 1962 when I came to CERN as a young post-doctoral fellow working at the University Institute of Theoretical Physics in Copenhagen (now the [[Niels Bohr Institute]]) to perform a [[nuclear emulsion]] experiment. During my visit in 1994, I was fascinated to see the exciting developments in [[physics]] that were taking place at CERN, and I had only one wish— that my own country, [[Pakistan]]— should somehow become involved in scientific collaboration with CERN, and that our [[physicist]]s and [[engineer]]s could also become part of the most advanced, challenging and rewarding scientific endeavour: the [[Large Hadron Collider]] (LHC).|sign=Ishfaq Ahmad, 1994|source=source<ref name="CERN"/>}}

In the 1990s, Ahmad played a pivotal role in building closer relations with the [[CERN]], and lobbied tirelessly for PAEC to reach an agreement with CERN.<ref name="CERN">{{Cite web
  | last =CERN Courier
  | author-link =CERN Courier
  | title =CERN and Pakistan: a personal perspective
  | website =CERN Courier services
  | date =5 October 2003
  | publisher =CERN
  | url =http://cerncourier.com/cws/article/cern/28934
  | format =cws
  | access-date =2014-03-26
  | archive-date =11 August 2011
  | archive-url =https://web.archive.org/web/20110811094528/http://cerncourier.com/cws/article/cern/28934
  | url-status =dead
  }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|title=People|journal=CERN Courier|date=July 1999|volume=39|issue=6|page=32|url=https://cds.cern.ch/record/1732967}}</ref> In 1997, Ahmad, as chair of PAEC, signed an agreement with CERN in the up gradation of the [[Compact Muon Solenoid|CMS]] detector and the financial contribution worth one million [[Swiss franc|SFr]] for the construction of eight magnetic rings for the detector.<ref name="CERN"/> This was followed by in 1998, Ishfaq Ahmad, as PAEC chairman, reached another contract with CERN.<ref name="CERN"/> The signing of the agreement was followed by the state visit of CERN's director [[Christopher Llewellyn Smith]] with whom Ahmad signed a collaborative agreement that provided an entry point for Pakistani's scientist (respectively PAEC) into the CMS collaboration.<ref name="CERN"/>

In 2000, another treaty between PAEC and CERN was signed that covered the construction of the resistive plate chambers required for the CMS muon system. In Press Conference with [[Luciano Maiani]], Ahmad quoted: "I very much hope and wish that these developments may eventually lead to Pakistan becoming an associate member of CERN."<ref>{{cite journal|title=CERN and Pakistan strengthen agreement|journal=CERN Courier|date=July 2000|volume=40|issue=6|page=9|url=https://cds.cern.ch/record/1733094}}</ref>

==Pakistan Atomic Energy Commission==
{{Main|Kirana Hills|Ras Koh Hills|Chagai Hills}}
{{See also|Chagai-I|Chagai-II}}

In 1960, Ahmad joined the [[Pakistan Atomic Energy Commission]] (PAEC) as senior scientist and was allowed to proceed abroad for post-doctoral work at several of the world's most renowned research institutions. Ahmad published papers in physics at the [[Niels Bohr Institute]] at [[Copenhagen]]; also at the [[University of Montreal]] in [[Canada]] as well as the [[Paris-Sorbonne University|University of Paris – Sorbonne]] in [[France]]. Finally, he settled down for work at the Lahore Centre of the [[Pakistan Atomic Energy Commission|PAEC]] (PAEC) in 1965. Ahmad held the post of Senior Scientific Officer until 1966.<ref name="Islamic Academy of Sciences">{{cite web|last=IAS|title=Prof. Ishfaq Ahmad|url=http://www.iasworld.org/profiles/4.html|website=Islamic Academy of Sciences|access-date=11 October 2012}}{{Dead link|date=October 2024 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref> From 1969 until 1971, Ahmad was the director of the Atomic Energy Centre in [[Lahore]]; and then served as secretary of [[Pakistan Atomic Energy Commission|PAEC]] from 1967 till 1969.<ref name="Islamic Academy of Sciences"/> In 1971, Ahmad became director of the [[Pakistan Institute of Nuclear Science and Technology|Institute of Nuclear Science and Technology]] in [[Nilore]] until 1976.<ref name="Islamic Academy of Sciences"/> In 1976, he became a Science Member of PAEC, raised to the position of Senior Member in 1988.  He became Chairman of the Commission in 1991 and remained its chairman from 13 March 1991 to 19 December 2001.<ref name="Islamic Academy of Sciences"/>

While he was Chairman PAEC, Ahmad has been heading the country's delegation at the [[International Atomic Energy Agency]] (IAEA) in [[Vienna]], [[Austria]].<ref name="IAEA archives">{{Cite web
  | last =IAEA archives
  | title =Technical cooperation with IAEA
  | publisher =IAEA archives
  | url =http://www.iaea.org/technicalcooperation/Home/Highlights-Archive/Archive-2005-Before/SAGTAC.html
  |access-date=2014-03-26}}</ref>
At IAEA, he was always very keen for getting technical support and the breaking of the isololation of scientists from third world. On his persuasion IAEA's technical assistance program was adapted to cater for special needs of the developing countries.<ref name="IAEA archives"/> In this regard a Standing Advisory Group on Technical Assistance and Cooperation (SAGTAC) was established; Ahmad served as the first Chairman of the Group.<ref name="IAEA archives"/>

===1971 war and atomic bomb project===

After the [[Indo-Pakistani War of 1971|1971 war]] with India, the government sent Ishfaq Ahmad to the [[Pakistan Institute of Nuclear Science and Technology]] (PINSTECH).<ref name="Islamic Academy of Sciences"/> When [[Munir Ahmad Khan]] became the chairman of PAEC and was put in charge of secret atomic bomb project, Munir Khan appointed Ahmad as the director of PINSTECH, where he remained up to 1976. Ahmad served as the director of the Nuclear Physics Division at the secret [[Pakistan Institute of Nuclear Science and Technology|Pinstech Institute]] which developed the first designs of [[atomic bomb]]s, a clandestine project during the [[Indo-Pakistani War of 1971|post-1971 war]].<ref name="Rahman 1999 71–72"/> There, he played an influential role in leading the physics and mathematical calculations in the [[critical mass]] of the weapons, and did preliminary theoretical work on the implosion method used in the weapons.<ref name="Rahman 1999 78–80"/>

In 1976, PAEC succeeded in producing the first local 10[[kilogram|kg]] of [[Yellowcake]]<ref>{{harv|Rehman|1999|pp=80–81}}</ref> and later on produced the <sup>239</sup>[[Plutonium-239|Pu]], the [[Weapons grade plutonium|weapon grade plutonium]] in 1983, which was later tested with the nuclear device.<ref>{{harv|Rehman|1999|pp=99–100}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web
 |last=Azam
 |first=Rai Muhammad Saleh
 |title=See: Kirana Hills: The Cold Tests
 |website=Defense Journal of Pakistan
 |date=June 2000
 |url=http://www.defencejournal.com/2000/june/chagai.htm
 |url-status=dead
 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120401181303/http://www.defencejournal.com/2000/june/chagai.htm
 |archive-date= 1 April 2012
}}
</ref>

At PINSTECH, Ahmad produced the first [[Photographic plate]] to identify the fissile matter in natural uranium when it is explored.<ref name="Science direct">{{Cite journal
  | last1 = Ahmad | first1 = Ishfaq
  | last2 = Khan | first2 =Hameed Ahmad
  | last3 = Akber | first3 =Riaz Ahmad
  | title =The use of Alpha Sensitive Plastic Films (ASPF) for uranium/thorium exploration and prospecting
  | journal =Radiation Physics and Chemistry
  | volume = 11
  | issue = 6
  | pages = 295–297
  | year =1978
  | doi =10.1016/0146-5724(78)90090-0
  | bibcode = 1978RaPC...11..295K }}</ref> However, due to its classified research, the knowledge of such detector is completely classified.<ref name="Science direct"/> The NPD developed the [[Thermoluminescent Dosimeter]] to measure the detection of alpha particles emitted in the decay of radon and thoron gases. Ahmad collaborating with Hameed Ahmad Khan —director of Radiation Physics Division – in the development of [[CR-39]], a type of particle detector.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Khan|first1=Hameed Ahmad|last2=Ahmad|first2=Ishfaq|year=1981|title=Radon/thoron detection properties of a CR-39 plastic track detector|journal=Nuclear Instruments and Methods in Physics Research|volume=185|issue=1–3|pages=401–405|bibcode=1981NIMPR.185..401K|doi=10.1016/0029-554X(81)91237-4}}</ref> Ahmad gained expertise in nuclear emulsion and developed a first classified nuclear emulsion that provided information about the mass, charge and velocity of the particles producing the track.<ref>{{Cite journal
  | last1 = Ahmad | first1 = Ishfaq
  | title =Track structure and identification of particles in nuclear emulsions
  | journal =Nuclear Instruments and Methods
  | volume = 173
  | issue = 1
  | pages = 15–20
  | date =June 1980
  | doi =10.1016/0029-554X(80)90564-9
  | bibcode = 1980NucIM.173...15A
}}</ref>

A first [[nuclear device|device]] was physically manufactured by 1983, and transported to [[Sargodha Airbase|Sargodha air force base]] for a first test.{{Citation needed|date=August 2013}} On 11 March 1983, a first cold test, codename [[Kirana-I]], of a device was secretly carried out at the weapon-testing laboratories built inside the Central Ammunition Depot (CAD) of Sargodha AFB. The test was overseen and conducted by a small team of scientists led by Ahmad, while calculations on quantum [[Quantum harmonic oscillator|oscillator]] was conducted by Theoretical physics group.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Sublette |first1=Carey |title=Pakistan's Nuclear Weapons Program - Development |url=http://nuclearweaponarchive.org/Pakistan/PakDevelop.html |website=nuclearweaponarchive.org}}</ref> Other invitees and attendees included the [[Munir Ahmad Khan]], Samar Mubarakmand, and Masud Ahmad of [[Pakistan Atomic Energy Commission|PAEC]] whilst others were high-ranking civilians officials of elite [[Pakistan Civil Services|civil bureaucracy]] and the active-duty officer of the [[Pakistan Armed Forces|Pakistan military]].

===Chagai tests===

In 1991, Ahmad was officially approved as the chairman of PAEC by the [[prime minister of Pakistan]] after Munir Khan retired. During this time, he had been a senior scientist and acted as official science advisor to the government of Pakistan on many occasions. In 1998, Ahmad visited [[Canada]] to deliver lecture on quantum physics at the Montreal Laboratory when the news of surprise nuclear tests, codename [[Pokhran-II]], of India reached to him. On 16 May 1998, Ahmad cut short his trip and returned to Pakistan to attend meeting with Prime minister [[Nawaz Sharif]], and arranged his meeting with Prime minister on 17 May 1998. The message was bestowed to him by the [[JS HQ (Pakistan)|Joint Headquarters]] at Rawalpindi, informing him to remain on stand-by a meeting with the Prime Minister.{{Citation needed|date=August 2013}} After commencing the meeting with the Prime minister, Ahmad received green signal from the government of Pakistan to conduct country's first test as a suitable reply to Indian nuclear aggression.

Ahmad personally supervised the test preparations as he also suggests the codenames of the tests. On 28 May 1998, the PAEC, sided by [[Kahuta Research Laboratories|KRL]] and [[Pakistan Army Corps of Engineers|corps of engineers]], performed the first nuclear tests, codename ''[[Chagai-I]]'' which was followed by ''[[Chagai-II]]'' two days later, in May 1998.<ref name="Nazaria-i-Pakistan Trust">{{Cite web
  | last1 =(NPT)
  | first1 =Ashfaque
  | author2 =Khalid Mahmood Asim
  | title =Dr. Ashfaque Ahmad
  | website =Prominent Scientists of Pakistan
  | publisher =Nazaria-i-Pakistan Trust
  | year =2003
  | url =http://nazariapak.info/famous-pakistanis/Scientists.html#Ashfaque
  | access-date =25 April 2010
  | archive-date =13 January 2010
  | archive-url =https://web.archive.org/web/20100113154236/http://www.nazariapak.info/famous-pakistanis/Scientists.html#Ashfaque
  | url-status =dead
  }}</ref> Evidently, the fission devices were had contained the boosted-fission [[High-enriched uranium|HEU]] nuclear process, that came from the [[A. Q. Khan Research Laboratories|KRL]]. But, on 30 May, the second test, codename [[Chagai-II]], was performed completely under the [[command and control]] management of the PAEC. The fission devices, on a second test, were reportedly had contained the weapon grade plutonium, producing around at ~20kt of nuclear force. All together, the [[Superposition principle|superposition]] of sum of the forces and the total blast [[Nuclear weapon yield|yield]] was ranged at the nearly ~40[[Kiloton|kt]] of [[nuclear force]], according to the PAEC scientific data.<ref name="(Pakistan's Leaders Online)">{{Citation
  | last =Ibid
  | first =(Pakistan's Leaders Online)
  | title =See
  | url =http://www.pakistanileaders.com.pk/profile/Dr_Ishfaq_Ahmad
  | access-date =28 April 2010
  | archive-date =3 January 2011
  | archive-url =https://web.archive.org/web/20110103060230/http://pakistanileaders.com.pk/profile/Dr_Ishfaq_Ahmad
  | url-status =dead
  }}</ref>

==Later work and activism==
===Earthquake studies and climate change===

After retiring from the PAEC in 2001, Ahmad developed interests in [[seismology]] and the [[climate change]], and helped founded the Global Change Impact Studies Centre and the [[Centre for Earthquake Studies]] (CES), both initially attached to the [[National Centre for Physics]] (NCP) in [[Islamabad]].

He also put Pakistan on the governing Council of the International Institute for Applied Systems Analysis (IIASA), Austria, which conducts policy related research using mathematical modeling and simulation tools.<ref>{{Cite web
 |last        = IIASA
 |first       = International Institute for Applied Systems Analysis
 |author-link  = International Institute for Applied Systems Analysis
 |title       = Council Member: Dr. Ahmad, Ishfaq
 |website        = IIASA-National Member Organization:Pakistan
 |publisher   = Directorate of National Member Organizations and Council Members
 |year        = 2009
 |url         = http://www.iiasa.ac.at/Admin/DI/docs/IIASA_NMO.html
 |url-status     = dead
 |archive-url  = https://web.archive.org/web/20050627082900/http://www.iiasa.ac.at/Admin/DI/docs/IIASA_NMO.html
 |archive-date = 27 June 2005}}
</ref>

===Global Change Impact Studies Centre (GCISC)===

Ishfaq Ahmad's efforts led to the creation of the Global Change Impact Studies Centre (GCISC). The centre, an autonomous organisation under the federal govt, works in collaboration with national institutions such as Pakistan Meteorological Department (PMD), National Agricultural Research Centre (NARC), WAPDA and PCRWR etc. The centre has also established collaborative relationship with international institutions, most importantly The Abdus Salam International Centre for Theoretical Physics (ICTP), Trieste, Italy.<ref>{{Cite web
  | last =(GCISC)
  | first =Global Change Impact Studies Centre
  | title =GCISC Advisory Committee
  | publisher =Global Change Impact Studies Centre
  | year =2006
  | url =http://www.gcisc.org.pk/advc.aspx
  | access-date =25 April 2010
  | archive-date =21 January 2010
  | archive-url =https://web.archive.org/web/20100121062531/http://www.gcisc.org.pk/advc.aspx
  | url-status =dead
  }}</ref>

===Centre for Earthquake Studies (CES)===

After 8 October 2005, [[2005 Kashmir earthquake|Kashmir earthquake]], the Government has decided to establish a Centre for Earthquake studies in Islamabad, under the technical direction of Ishfaq Ahmad.
The centre under the directorship of Mr. Shahid Ashraf and Ahsan Mubarak started work in collaboration with world leading scientists such as Elchin Khalilov of Azerbaijan. The centre conducts research using a Gravitational Wave Recorder housed at the National Centre for Physics, Islamabad.

===Advocacy for Nuclear power===

Ishfaq Ahmad is internationally known for his long-standing public advocacy for the [[nuclear power plant]]s for the industrial and socio-economic growth.<ref name="IAEA Sustainable Development: A Role for Nuclear Power?">{{citation |title=The Future Role of Nuclear Power in Member States |work=Sustainable Development: A Role for Nuclear Power? |publisher=IAEA Sustainable Development: A Role for Nuclear Power? |date=28–29 September 1999}}<!--|url=The Future Role of Nuclear Power in Member States|accessdate=12 October 2012--></ref><ref name="Daily Times">{{cite web |last=Staff reports |title='Nuclear power programme meets |url=http://www.dailytimes.com.pk/default.asp?page=story_26-3-2005_pg7_43|work=Daily Times|access-date=12 October 2012}}</ref> On international forums, Ahmad deterred the international pressure mounted on Pakistan after conducting its tests, instead highlighted the achievements gained by Pakistan on its [[Nuclear power in Pakistan|nuclear power]] infrastructure in the country as well as the need of Pakistan's usage of nuclear power for its economical growth.<ref>{{cite journal|last=Ahmad|first=Ishfaq|title=Statement by Dr. Ishfaq Ahmad. Leader of the Pakistan Delegation to the 44th IAEA General Conference. Vienna|journal=IAEA Press Release|date=18–22 September 2000|url=https://docs.google.com/viewer?a=v&q=cache:RzK6UGQz3VUJ:www.iaea.org/About/Policy/GC/GC44/Statements/pakistan.pdf+Ishfaq+Ahmad+IAEA&hl=en&gl=us&pid=bl&srcid=ADGEESgaQPUlDJI3Lrdm00zJB68mD6zhq9l0ADIhHJyeURlzNXpZrl1nMS9Irnly3UzZTeHuGumrL8NsPbayRcFE-jrGQLIOMOa1CMWjnxaT4xXfvj2uj5pHFcurBqkBY0tkd7QoLEDN&sig=AHIEtbTHh-qLggGITTqhLqrN0GUaxf39dQ|access-date=12 October 2012|format=google docs}}</ref> In 2012, Ahmad lobbied for the HMC-3 consortium to be listed as first commercial nuclear power corporation and helped the consortium to acquire its first license to manufacture nuclear materials for industrial power plants.<ref name="The News International">{{cite news|last=Anis|first=Mohammad|title=HMC-3 gets licence to produce parts for N-plants|url=http://www.thenews.com.pk/Todays-News-13-17892-HMC-3-gets-licence-to-produce-parts-for-N-plants|access-date=12 October 2012|newspaper=The News International|date=3 October 2012|author5=The News International}}</ref>

==State honours, awards and recognition==

In 1989, Ishfaq Ahmad was bestowed with first state honour, ''[[Sitara-e-Imtiaz]]'' by [[Benazir Bhutto]]; and [[Hilal-e-Imtiaz]] in 1995.<ref name="The Office of Pakistan Academy of Sciences"/> In 1998, Ahmad received the highest state honour, [[Nishan-e-Imtiaz]], given to any national of Pakistan, for his services to the country in a graceful state ceremony.<ref name="The Office of Pakistan Academy of Sciences"/> The same year, he was awarded gold medallion by the [[Institute of Leadership & Management, Lahore|Institute of Leadership and Management]] in Lahore.
* [[Nishan-i-Imitiaz]] (1998)
* [[Hilal-i-Imtiaz]] (1995)
* [[Sitara-i-Imtiaz]] (1989)
* [[Gold Medal]], [[Pakistan Academy of Sciences]] (1998)
* [[Gold Medal]], [[Institute of Leadership & Management, Lahore|Institute of Leadership & Management]] (ILM) (1998)
* [[Gold Medal]], Society of Engineering, Materials and Metallurgical Engineering (SEMME), Karachi, (1998)
* [[Gold Medal]], Geological Society of Punjab, (1998)
* [[Doctorate of Science]] [[Honoris Causa]], [[University of Engineering and Technology, Lahore|UET Lahore]], 2000.
* Who's who in atom, American Institute of Physics (1969)
